title: Evaluation of the unary open coefficient map
statement:
The following fully quantified Lean statement is the unary/finite component in the support-coordinate argument. All operations and normalizations are those of [def-sf-operation-stages], and its explicit coordinate maps are those of [def-sf-integral-projection-factor-evaluation-data] and [def-sf-integral-projection-middle-map].

theorem integralProjectionOpenFactorEvaluation
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (C : D.CoefficientDatum)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic C.l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic C.l) E] (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (S : SixFunctorOperationDatum D C E n hn) (hl : IsUnit (C.l : D.k))
    (o : Operations C.l E) (z : Realizations C.l E D o)
    {X Y : SixFunctorSpace D} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [QuasiCompact f.hom.left]
    (c : Compactification f.hom.left) (m : ℕ)
    (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory C.l E X.obj.left) :
    (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation C.l E c.Z m).map
        (ProjectionFactors.openReduction D C E n hn S hl o z f c K) ≫
      ((o.openEvaluation c.i).evaluation m).hom.app
        ((calculus C.l E X.obj.left).reduction.obj K.obj) ≫
      (sfIntrinsicExtensionByZero c.i
        (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing C.l E (m + 1))).mapDerivedCategory.map
          (((calculus C.l E X.obj.left).reductionEvaluation m).hom.app K.obj) =
    ((calculus C.l E c.Z).reductionEvaluation m).hom.app
        (((S.higher.integralExchange (identitySquare f c)).stage.openExtension.obj K).obj) ≫
      (FactorEvaluation.extension D C E n hn S f c m K).hom

prop-sf-pf-coherence.proof.md, compatibility with j_!;
def-sf-operation-stages, openProjection, and the canonical open-unit scalar mate.

proof.text: Use integral_residue_tor to obtain finiteTorConstructibleIntegral for K from its constructibility. Apply openReconstructionEffectivity to the quasi-compact open immersion c.i. This supplies invertibility of the specified whole-system openReduction component, which is the map inverted in ProjectionFactors.openReduction.

Unfold FactorEvaluation.extensionIso. The openProjection field of S.integralNormalization identifies its component with scalar reduction of the specified openRealization followed by sixFunctorIntegralOpenReduction. This last map is definitionally openFiniteReduction: both consist of finiteReductionIso inverse, openComparison, localized finiteOpenIso, and finite extension of finiteReductionIso.

Apply integralOpenFiniteEvaluation to the actual c.i, realizationModel, K.obj and m. It identifies openEvaluation followed by finite extension of reductionEvaluation with evaluation of the whole-system openReduction followed by target reductionEvaluation and openFiniteReduction. Substitute this identity into the desired equation.

Expand ProjectionFactors.openReduction and FactorEvaluation.extension. Functoriality and associativity place evaluation of the inverse openReduction immediately before evaluation of openReduction; cancel these maps using the invertibility from step 1. Apply naturality of reductionEvaluation first to openRealization and then to the eqToHom induced by the stage.openExtension equality. The result is exactly the right-hand composite. No faithfulness of evaluation and no equality inferred from finite evaluations is used.

proof_origin.place: Compatibility with j_!: finite open mate evaluation, cancellation of the specified whole-system reduction, and naturality through the prescribed stage and realization comparisons. W6 uses the existing generic integralOpenFiniteEvaluation theorem; no new split.
